primary_claim: Adding a KL-divergence variational term (vSAE) to a TopK sparse autoencoder does not improve interpretability and degrades reconstruction performance relative to a standard TopK SAE, primarily because the KL pressure kills a large fraction of features (e.g. only about half alive at k=256), though the vSAE shows somewhat improved robustness on spurious-correlation-removal and targeted-probe-perturbation metrics

effect.metric: SAEBench quality metrics (KL divergence, cross-entropy loss, explained variance, cosine similarity) and fraction of living features, TopK vs. vSAE TopK
effect.value: TopK consistently outperforms vSAE TopK on reconstruction/quality metrics across all K tested; vSAE has a low fraction of living features (e.g. only ~half alive at k=256); vSAE shows somewhat better Spurious Correlation Removal (SCR) and Targeted Probe Perturbation (TPP) robustness scores

contradicts_or_qualifies: their own prior preliminary hypothesis/findings (referenced in the project's earlier proposal) that VSAE consistently outperforms standard SAEs in feature disentanglement; this post's controlled experiments instead find vSAE underperforms standard TopK SAE on most quality metrics
stated_future_work: augment the vSAE architecture/loss/hyperparameters to reduce the pressure that kills features, to see if more live features recover the performance drop
run experiments on a larger model such as Pythia-70M instead of only the 1-layer GeLU network
increase the number of activations used in the tSNE analysis to activate a greater number of features
limitations_stated: only ran experiments on a 1-layer GeLU network due to time and memory constraints; such a small transformer can only embed bigram/trigram statistics
due to memory constraints, only features that fired on a subset of the dataset were used in the tSNE global analysis
synthetic (activation-maximizing) tokens for feature interpretation seemed unrelated to the real dataset examples that caused the features to fire
purely applying variational methods without TopK led to poor results, since KL divergence alone was not a strong enough sparsity regularizer
quote: We ultimately find that this addition does not benefit the interpretability of the language model and degrades performance.
